justification: The evidence shows the system maintains high validation accuracy under several predefined perturbations and has a functioning out-of-distribution mechanism that detected most excluded-class samples; the reported results were also independently reproduced. This supports some operational robustness for the described document-classification workflow. However, the evidence is limited to validation tests and does not directly demonstrate robustness in live deployment conditions or across the full range of operational variation.
evidence_used: With 10% randomly removed non-critical fields, accuracy was 93.7%.
With the predefined OCR degradation transformation, accuracy was 92.1%.
Across the predefined formatting-variation set, accuracy ranged from 91.6% to 94.8%.
Of the 1,200 out-of-distribution samples, 1,127 were flagged by the out-of-distribution mechanism.
The validation protocol contains three predefined perturbation tests; corresponding accuracies were 92.8%, 90.9%, and 93.4%.
A separate validation team reproduced the reported tests.
limitations: Evidence is based on predefined validation perturbations rather than observed operational deployment.
No direct evidence is provided for performance under unlisted or more severe real-world document variations.
The out-of-distribution test results do not specify false positive behavior or performance on in-distribution edge cases.
Staff review before downstream processing may mitigate risk, but the extent of that mitigation is not quantified in the evidence.
